segments.text: Disciplined people may not be using more willpower.
You wait to feel motivated. The feeling shows up late, or never, and the task stays untouched.
A 2015 paper ran six studies with 2,274 people in total. Those with better self-control relied more on habits, and reported less effort holding themselves back.
A practical way to try this. One: pick a fixed cue, like right after breakfast. Two: shrink the task to two minutes. Three: start the moment the cue happens.
These results were linked, not proven, and mostly self-reported. Habits take time to form.
Try it today: pick one cue, and do two minutes after it.
